contexts.text: Brass () = natural good. AC 425. AC 426. AC 2162:6. AC 2576:6. AC 2576:7. AC 2967:3. AC 3708:12. AC 3863:5. AC 4489:2. AC 4677:9. AC 6432:2. AC 9050:9. AC 9391:2. AR 775, Illustrated. AE 70, Illustrated.
The inmost Celestial they compared to gold, the lower Celestial to brass, and the lowest or corporeal thence to wood. Illustrated.
They compared lower or natural goods to brass.
The age of brass was the time of the Church which followed the Ancient Church.
For brass gold () = for natural good celestial good... For wood brass = for corporeal good natural good. AE 176:3.
The shoe brass () = natural good.
Hence their lavers were of brass, as also that great one called the brazen sea (), because brass represented the good of outward worship, which is the same as natural good. AC 3147:6.
Belly and thighs of brass () = the third state of the Church, which was one of natural good. AC 9406:7. AC 10030:3. AE 176:2.
Under Serpent, see these references. AE 70:end.
Brass = the good of love and of charity in the Natural.
Brass () = natural good which will be strong against evils.
And brass () = external good. Brass = natural good, or what is the same, external good, which is the good of the external or natural man. AC 10332.
Thou shalt make fifty taches of brass () = a full capacity of conjunction from external good.
Under Base, see this reference, and at AC 9748. AC 9770. AC 10236. AC 10236:7.
Thou shalt overlay it with brass () = a representative of what is good. Brass = natural or external good, and overlaying with brass was a representative of that good.
All the vessels thereof thou shalt make of brass () = all things from good. AC 9727.
All the pins of the court shall be of brass () = all things conjoining and steadying both Heavens, the middle and the ultimate, by means of good... Brass = external good.
Goods and truths from self and not from the Lord are signified by possessing gold, silver, and brass in their girdles ().
The vessel of brass () = a doctrinal in which there is good.
Thou shalt make a laver of brass () = the good of the natural man in which purification takes place.
They who were in natural good received these things holily; hence those times were called brazen, for brass = such good.
A vessel of brass () = the Scientific from natural good.
The twigs became shining brass with gold tips.
Brass = natural good, which is the ultimate good... The third age was called brazen or copper, because natural good then reigned, which is what is just and sincere of moral life.
The shoe iron and brass () = the lowest Natural from truth and good.
Copper or brass = the good of the external or natural man.
Walls of brass () = good protecting.
Burnished brass () = good in the Natural.
Mountains of brass () = the good of love in the natural man. AE 405:22.
Vessels of brass () = the truths of natural good.

Belly and thighs of brass = the Church which succeeded the ancient spiritual Church, and which may be called spiritual natural; in it there reigned the good of faith and truth from that good; this good is signified in the Word by brass, and also by the belly and thighs.
That the ultimate of the Word is natural truth and good is signified by thy shoe iron and brass.
Under Censer, see this reference.

The things of the sense of the letter of the Word are signified by brass, tin, iron, and lead (), because by these are signified the goods and truths of the natural man, for which man are those things of the Word which are contained in the sense of its letter.
When (false doctrine) is confirmed by means of the natural things of the Word, such as are those of the sense of its letter, the idol then becomes of brass and stone ().
Brass () = good in ultimates; here, evils.
Vessels of iron and brass () = Knowledges of natural truth and good.
Vessels of brass () = the knowledge of good in the natural man.
